correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the crown Ehrhart counts as a transfer-matrix trace and independently verified small counts by direct integer-coordinate enumeration. The exact binomial generating transform gives F3 and F4. Rank 3 follows by the reciprocal-quartic y=z+1/z reduction. Rank 4 follows from an independently regenerated degree-nine discriminant 16D, the exact Sturm variation sequence 6,6,5,5,4,4,3,3 isolating every real D zero, and exact Sturm negative-root counts 4,6,4 at λ=-32,0,9. Constant monic/constant coefficient prevents root crossing 0 or ∞; negative z² coefficient eliminates λ beyond the last discriminant root. The delivered verifier executes from the embedded file. No finite scan is used as an infinite-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected all-rank 2026 source proves the real-rootedness of the same wheel–whirl pencil only on the convex interpolation segment [0,1], and older sources provide definitions and coefficient formulae. The new statement gives the mathematically distinct maximal parameter set on the entire real line in the two smallest ranks, with sharp algebraic collision parameters and a change from unbounded to bounded negative stability. Targeted research-record and primary-literature searches did not identify an equivalent or stronger result; residual priority uncertainty is acknowledged.
residual_risks: External indexing and accessible own records are not exhaustive; a separate unindexed root-pencil calculation could exist.
The result is a polynomial-pencil theorem: only λ=0 and λ=1 are necessarily polytopal Ehrhart numerators; all other parameters have no claimed polytope realization.
For r≥5, no maximal interval or general lower bound is claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating real-rootedness theorem naturally invites a sharp stability-domain question for the wheel–whirl relaxation polynomial pencil. This result gives a complete two-rank classification over all real perturbations, identifies two exact algebraic stability endpoints in the first nonreciprocal case, and proves the qualitative transition from an unbounded left extension at r=3 to a finite one at r=4. These exact invariants provide benchmarks for sharp extensions and interlacing mechanisms; they are not arbitrary rounded samples or routine substitution variants.
